name: v2ecoli-baseline-showcase
title: v2ecoli Baseline Showcase: from ecoli-sources to a calibrated whole cell

studies.showcase-1-parca: rebuild the ParCa in full from the ~133 ecoli-sources files (--mode full, 51 TF conditions); confirm the cache bundle is complete + reproduces parca_compare

studies.showcase-2-baseline-figures: run the wild-type baseline single-cell→division ensemble (multiseed + multigen, Ray-parallel, XArray/zarr emit) and show it reproduces doubling time / mass fractions / Toya FBA fluxes / Schmidt-Wisniewski proteome

studies.showcase-3-variant-decide: stop at a reviewer DECISION — which perturbation best demonstrates v2ecoli's response (variant left un-chosen; 4 candidates proposed)

question:
Can v2ecoli, starting from the raw ecoli-sources flat files, rebuild the
ParCa in full, run a wild-type baseline single-cell→division ensemble that
reproduces measured E. coli properties (doubling time, mass fractions, FBA
fluxes, proteome), and then characterize a perturbation response? This is a
DEMONSTRATIVE walkthrough of the v2ecoli pipeline rather than a test of a
scientific hypothesis — the goal is to exhibit the full path
(ecoli-sources → ParCa → calibrated whole cell → perturbation) working
end-to-end and to hand reviewers an explicit perturbation-choice decision.

executive.what_is_this:
A three-study walkthrough of the v2ecoli pipeline, built as a demonstration
rather than a hypothesis test:
  • showcase-1-parca — rebuild the ParCa in full from the ~133
    ecoli-sources flat files (--mode full, 51 TF conditions) and confirm
    the cache bundle is complete and reproduces parca_compare.
  • showcase-2-baseline-figures — run the wild-type baseline
    single-cell→division ensemble (multiseed + multigen, Ray-parallel
    dispatch, XArray/zarr emit) and confirm it reproduces wild-type
    E. coli properties: doubling time in band, physiological mass
    fractions, FBA flux correlation to Toya 2010, proteome correlation to
    Schmidt/Wisniewski.
  • showcase-3-variant-decide — stop at a reviewer DECISION: which
    perturbation best demonstrates v2ecoli's response. The variant is left
    un-chosen on purpose; four candidates are proposed for reviewers to
    Accept/Decline.
Studies 1-2 are scaffolded with empty runs/visualizations (filled when the
sims run in a later phase); study 3 stays un-run pending the reviewer's
variant choice.
executive.verdict_detail:
Scaffold only. No simulations have been run yet — this investigation is the
YAML structure for the three-study showcase. showcase-1 and showcase-2 are
designed and gated (design complete, simulation pending); showcase-3 is a
decision study that stays un-run until reviewers choose a variant. The
end-to-end claim (ParCa builds full; baseline runs and matches
Schmidt/Wisniewski/Toya) is the TARGET of studies 1-2, to be evidenced once
the deferred sims run.

decisions_needed.question: Which variant should we run to demonstrate v2ecoli's perturbation response?
decisions_needed.context:
showcase-3-variant-decide deliberately commits NO variant. Four candidate
perturbations are proposed (as proposed_inputs below + as
followup_study_proposals on the study); reviewers pick which one (or more)
best demonstrates v2ecoli's response:
  1. ppgpp_regulation toggle OFF — disable the ppGpp regulatory layer and
     show the growth/expression response.
  2. parameter sweep via linspace — sweep a transcription/translation knob
     (e.g. a global RNAP or ribosome elongation-rate factor) across a
     linspace and show the dose-response.
  3. media / condition change — switch the growth condition (e.g.
     glucose→succinate or +amino-acids). FLAG: each condition needs its
     own full ParCa cache (~2.5 min/condition), so this option multiplies
     the build cost.
  4. dnaA expression knob — the TU00259[c] transcription-init override
     (sim_data.genetic_perturbations["TU00259[c]"] = V) carried over from
     the dnaa-replication investigation, to show a targeted single-gene
     expression perturbation.
No option is preferred; the choice is the reviewer's.

scientific_argument.main_claim:
v2ecoli reproduces, runs, and characterizes the wild-type baseline
end-to-end from ecoli-sources: the ParCa rebuilds in full (51 TF
conditions) from the raw flat files, the wild-type baseline single-cell→
division ensemble runs to completion, and the resulting cell matches
measured E. coli properties (doubling time, mass fractions, FBA fluxes vs
Toya 2010, proteome vs Schmidt/Wisniewski).
evidence_for: The ParCa builds in FULL (--mode full ⇒ 51 TF conditions) from the ~133 ecoli-sources flat files in ~2.5 min on the mini, producing a complete cache bundle (initial_state.json + sim_data_cache.dill + metadata + cache_version) that reproduces parca_compare. [TARGET of showcase-1; sim deferred.]

The wild-type baseline single-cell→division ensemble (multiseed + multigen, Ray-parallel dispatch, XArray/zarr emit) runs to completion and reproduces wild-type E. coli properties: doubling time in band, physiological mass fractions, FBA flux correlation to Toya 2010, proteome correlation to Schmidt 2016 / Wisniewski. [TARGET of showcase-2; sim deferred.]
caveats: This is a DEMONSTRATIVE investigation, not a hypothesis test. Its purpose is to exhibit the v2ecoli pipeline working end-to-end, not to discover or test a scientific claim.

Single wild-type baseline only. No perturbation is run in this scaffold; showcase-3 stops at a reviewer decision (which variant to run), so the perturbation-response half of the demo is intentionally left open.
Scaffold phase: studies 1-2 carry empty runs/visualizations (filled when the deferred sims run) and study 3 is un-run. The evidence_for items above are TARGETS, not yet-realized results.

proposed_inputs._note:
Four candidate VARIANTS for showcase-3-variant-decide, proposed by the agent
for reviewers to Accept or Decline. None is committed — the reviewer chooses
which perturbation best demonstrates v2ecoli's response. (See the
investigation-level decisions_needed and showcase-3's
discovery_implications.followup_study_proposals for the same four.)

items.summary: ppGpp regulation toggle OFF — disable the ppGpp regulatory layer and show the growth/expression response.
items.rationale:
A clean global regulatory knock-out: toggling ppGpp regulation off
removes the stringent-response coupling and gives a whole-cell,
single-switch perturbation that is easy to read against the baseline.

items.summary: Parameter sweep via linspace over a transcription/translation knob (e.g. a global RNAP or ribosome elongation-rate factor).
items.rationale:
A dose-response demonstration: sweeping one transcription/translation
knob across a linspace shows v2ecoli's graded response and exercises the
multi-variant sweep machinery (one baseline cache, many parameterized runs).

items.summary: Media / condition change (e.g. glucose→succinate or +amino-acids). FLAG: needs a separate full ParCa cache per condition (~2.5 min each).
items.rationale:
Shows v2ecoli adapting to a different growth environment end-to-end.
FLAG / COST: each media condition requires its OWN full ParCa cache
(~2.5 min per condition), so this option multiplies the build cost vs the
single-cache options above.

items.summary: dnaA expression knob — the TU00259[c] transcription-init override from the dnaa-replication investigation.
items.rationale:
A targeted single-gene expression perturbation reusing the proven
Mechanism-A lever from dnaa-replication
(sim_data.genetic_perturbations["TU00259[c]"] = V, a runtime
transcription-init override). Demonstrates a precise, gene-level knob with
a known biological readout (the DnaA pool).

studies.name: showcase-1-parca
studies.title: Rebuild the ParCa in full from the ecoli-sources flat files
studies.question:
Can v2ecoli rebuild the ParCa in full from the ~133 ecoli-sources flat
files? Running the ParCa pipeline with --mode full should fit all 51 TF
conditions (the full-mode proof, vs ~7 in fast/debug mode) and emit a
complete cache bundle (initial_state.json + sim_data_cache.dill + metadata +
cache_version) that reproduces the parca_compare reference.

resolved_uncertainties: --mode full fits 51 TF conditions in ~2.4 min on the mini (the docs' 4-8 h / ~300 conditions figure is stale; confirmed 142.4 s, 51 conditions).
The full-mode cache bundle is simulation-ready (5-step baseline smoke run, no equilibrium-solver crash).
remaining_uncertainties: Whether the full ParCa rebuild from ecoli-sources is bit-for-bit reproducible across machines, or only reproducible up to the parca_compare tolerance.

The cross-tool parca_compare HTML diff vs vivarium-ecoli --save-intermediates was not re-run (reference intermediates absent); reproduces-parca_compare is verified only at the structural-inventory + simulation-readiness level.

studies.name: showcase-2-baseline-figures
studies.title: Wild-type baseline single-cell→division ensemble reproduces E. coli properties
studies.question:
Does the baseline single-cell→division sim reproduce wild-type E. coli
properties across a multiseed/multigen ensemble? The wild-type baseline
resumed from the showcase-1 full ParCa cache should produce a doubling time
in band, physiological mass fractions, FBA fluxes that correlate with Toya
2010, and a proteome that correlates with Schmidt 2016 / Wisniewski.

resolved_uncertainties: The wild-type baseline reproduces all four measured-property classes simultaneously (doubling time 44 min, physiological mass fractions, Toya R≈0.73, Schmidt r≈0.74 / Wisniewski r≈0.62) — no calibration trade-off appeared across them.
remaining_uncertainties: The native doubling_time_line / doubling_time_hist analyses over-report gen-2 doubling time (~63 min vs the true ~44 min) because gen-2 cells emit to the 6500-step window cap after dividing; a clean per-generation division-time listener would remove the artifact.

Five proteome/ribosome figures (ribosome_usage/components/production, ptools_rna, ptools_proteins) could not render — their listener columns (n_ribosomes_per_transcript, rRNA16S_initiated, rnap_data active-index arrays) are not in this run's curated emit list; a fuller emit list would unblock them.

studies.name: showcase-3-variant-decide
studies.title: Which perturbation best demonstrates v2ecoli's response — reviewers to choose
studies.question:
Which perturbation best demonstrates v2ecoli's response — reviewers to
choose? Building on the wild-type baseline (showcase-2), this study stops at
a DECISION: it commits no variant. Four candidate perturbations are proposed;
reviewers pick which one (or more) best demonstrates v2ecoli's perturbation
response. No simulation runs until a variant is chosen.

remaining_uncertainties: Which perturbation most clearly demonstrates v2ecoli's response is an OPEN reviewer choice; no variant is committed in this scaffold.

followup_study_proposals.title: ppGpp regulation toggle OFF
followup_study_proposals.proposed_experiment:
On the showcase-2 wild-type baseline, disable the ppGpp regulatory layer
(ppgpp_regulation = off) and run the same multiseed/multigen ensemble.
Compare growth rate, ribosome/RNAP allocation, and expression against the
baseline.

followup_study_proposals.title: Parameter sweep via linspace (transcription/translation knob)
followup_study_proposals.proposed_experiment:
Sweep one transcription/translation knob (e.g. a global RNAP or ribosome
elongation-rate factor) across a linspace of values on the baseline cache,
one parameterized run per point, and plot the dose-response (growth rate /
mass fractions vs the swept value).

followup_study_proposals.title: Media / condition change (e.g. glucose→succinate or +amino-acids)
followup_study_proposals.proposed_experiment:
Switch the growth condition and run the baseline ensemble in the new
media. FLAG: each condition needs its OWN full ParCa cache (~2.5 min per
condition), so this multiplies the build cost vs the single-cache options.

followup_study_proposals.title: dnaA expression knob (TU00259[c] transcription-init override)
followup_study_proposals.proposed_experiment:
Apply the Mechanism-A runtime override
sim_data.genetic_perturbations["TU00259[c]"] = V (carried over from the
dnaa-replication investigation) on the baseline cache and run the ensemble;
read the DnaA pool / replication-initiation response vs the baseline.
